cases.title: Final year project: campus bus tracking
cases.description: Our final-year group has to build a campus bus tracking system for the college. The college runs eleven bus routes and students never know where their bus is, so the idea is a small web app and a driver app that shares the bus position every few seconds. The professor wants a requirements document first, then a database design with at least eight tables (buses, routes, stops, drivers, students, trips, notifications, feedback), then the working prototype, then a short user test with ten students and a written report. For the backend I want to use Node and PostgreSQL because we learnt them in the web course. The driver app can be a simple page that uses the phone's GPS. The student page shows a map with the bus moving, the next stop and an estimated arrival time. We have never used maps before so we need to compare two or three map libraries. We also need login for students and drivers, an admin page to add routes and stops, and notifications when the bus is five minutes away. The notification part is optional but the professor said it would give extra marks. Security matters: drivers must only update their own bus, and student locations must never be stored. The report must have an introduction, literature review of at least six papers on public transport tracking, the design, the implementation, the testing results, and a conclusion with future work. The demo is in six weeks and the report is due one week later. Two of us are weak in front-end work and one is away for the next two weeks for a family function. Testing needs unit tests for the arrival-time calculation, integration tests for the API, and the user test with ten students who each complete five tasks while we time them and note problems.
